THE PROBLEM

How many calendars does a family need to manage one week?

Work
School
Sports
Doctors
Meetings
Pick-ups
Appointments

The problem isn't that families lack calendars. The problem is everything that happens between those calendars — noticing a conflict, finding who's free, texting, calling, rescheduling, remembering what's next.

That's the mental load of family coordination. It doesn't stay home — it follows parents into their workday, eating focus and time.

THE INSIGHT

Calendars show conflicts.
They don't solve them.

Today, families juggle calendars, messaging apps, phone calls and video calls — disconnected tools that leave all the coordination work on their shoulders.

THE SOLUTION

Meet Mia, your family's coordination assistant.

Mia doesn't just show the schedule — she reads it, finds the conflicts inside it, and acts on them.
